result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers explain the failures well and tie each rewrite to the actual submission. A's rewrite for the missing-customers query is the better teaching comment: it has the student compare row counts and work out which join type keeps unmatched rows. B just tells the student to use a LEFT JOIN. B's rewrites are tighter and closer to what a TA would really write, but A's lead on the most important teaching point outweighs its extra length. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers explain clearly why the original comments fail. Both also catch that "needs improvement on joins" is factually wrong. B's rewrite for the missing-customers query teaches better: it has the student compare row counts and work out the join type themselves. But B's rewrites are long, with bullets, office-hours invitations and career asides, so few TAs would actually leave them. A's rewrites are concise, respectful and specific, though A states the LEFT JOIN fix outright and leaves an awkward bracketed placeholder in rewrite #2.
